tier_reason: Upgraded from D to C: the benchmark page does carry numbers (a libheif user's 42 ms vs 30 ms whole-step times, libheif's own yuv2rgb vs libyuv, with no hardware, compiler, flags or code), and the libswscale numbers exist only in search snippets of blocked ffmpeg-devel threads, which caps them at C. No public benchmark code comparing libyuv with libswscale was found; libyuv's own unittests (docs/getting_started.md, LIBYUV_REPEAT) time its SIMD paths only against its own C fallback.

corrections.claimed_speedup: libheif issue #1215 (a user report, no hardware stated): YUV420 HEVC multi-tile decode to interleaved RGB took 42 ms with the ffmpeg decoder plugin plus libheif's own yuv2rgb conversion vs 30 ms with the same decoder plugin plus libyuv for the conversion, about 1.4x for the whole step (derived from page data); since the decoder is the same, the 12 ms difference comes from the conversion (derived from page data). Against libswscale, search snippets only (ffmpeg-devel threads, blocked here): about 4.19 s for libswscale vs 0.93 s for libyuv (about 4-5x) scaling a 1088x1920 BGR24 frame to 480x854 YUV420P 500 times on a MacBook Pro (2016), and about 10x on an Apple M1 for unscaled RGBA to YUV420P, still about 5x after FFmpeg's aarch64 NEON optimizations.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 930 stars and 302 forks on this unofficial GitHub mirror (its description says to submit issues and PRs upstream); upstream is chromium.googlesource.com/libyuv/libyuv, and README.chromium marks it shipped and security-critical in Chromium.
corrections.caveats: The libswscale comparison rests on search snippets of ffmpeg-devel threads ('Why not integrate libyuv as a scale filter' and the June 2024 'swscale modernization proposal'), which this sandbox cannot open (ffmpeg.org pipermail, narkive, mail-archive and patchwork are blocked), so the numbers, hardware and swscale settings are unverified. In the same threads FFmpeg developers replied that libswscale defaults to a higher-quality scaler, that comparable speed is reachable by tuning its flags, and that libyuv does no dithering or advanced filtering, so the gap partly reflects quality settings; the snippet numbers may also predate later swscale work. The libheif numbers compare against libheif's own converter, not libswscale, are whole-step times, and state no hardware, compiler or code. No public benchmark code comparing libyuv with libswscale was found; libyuv's unittests benchmark only its SIMD paths against its own C code. The incumbent role is better documented by sparkyuv, yuvutils-rs and xxYUV, which benchmark against libyuv and beat it only on some paths. This GitHub repo is an unofficial mirror; upstream is Chromium's libyuv on googlesource. BSD-3-Clause with a separate Google PATENTS grant.
